harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built a strongSwan (swanctl) IPsec site-to-site tunnel between node1 and node2 (OPNsense firewalls) over their shared transit network, carrying node3's private LAN (10.0.1.0/24) and node4's private LAN (10.0.2.0/24) so they reach each other by private address with traffic encrypted in transit. Verified with tcpdump that only ESP packets cross the transit link. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes with confirmed boot-identity changes and post-restart recovery.
actions_performed: Determined actual physical topology via ARP/L2 adjacency probing (initial interface-name assumptions were wrong): node1.vtnet1<->node2.vtnet1 = transit; node1.vtnet2<->node3.eth1 = lan-a; node2.vtnet2<->node4.eth1 = lan-b

Assigned OPNsense interfaces via config.xml + php rc.reload_all: node1 opt1=LAN_A 10.0.1.1/24, opt2=TRANSIT 10.10.10.1/30; node2 opt1=LAN_B 10.0.2.1/24, opt2=TRANSIT 10.10.10.2/30, while preserving the default LAN allow-any rule so SSH/exec access to both firewalls was never lost
Generated a PSK on node1 with openssl and transferred it to node2 via a transient local python http.server on the management LAN, avoiding printing the secret in any tool output

Wrote OPNsense/Swanctl config.xml entries (Connections/Connection, locals/local, remotes/remote, children/child) for an IKEv2 PSK site-to-site tunnel with local_ts/remote_ts covering each private subnet, plus an OPNsense/IPsec preSharedKeys entry, on both firewalls

Added firewall pass rules for UDP 500/4500 + ESP on the transit interface, allow-any on each private interface, and discovered/fixed the enc0 IPsec pseudo-interface registration (pluginctl -i) so the enc0 pass rule for decrypted tunnel traffic loaded correctly
Enabled and started strongSwan on both firewalls (legacy ipsec.enable=1 + pluginctl -c ipsec); confirmed IKE_SA ESTABLISHED and CHILD_SA INSTALLED with live byte/packet counters matching test traffic

Configured static addressing and cross-routes on node3/node4 (10.0.1.2/24 and 10.0.2.2/24, each routing to the other's subnet via its local OPNsense gateway) and persisted them in /etc/network/interfaces so they survive reboot
Verified end-to-end encrypted reachability: node3 <-> node4 ping succeeds over private addresses; tcpdump on the transit link shows only ESP packets, no plaintext leakage

Captured healthy baselines (kern.boottime for node1/node2, /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id for node3/node4) then restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time via native reboot mechanisms, polled each back online, and confirmed changed boot identity plus full recovery of interfaces, IPsec SAs, routes, and end-to-end connectivity after each restart

evidence.requirement: IPsec tunnel established between node1 and node2
evidence.summary: swanctl --list-sas on node1 shows IKE_SA ESTABLISHED and CHILD_SA INSTALLED (AES_GCM_16-128) between 10.10.10.1 and 10.10.10.2 with local_ts 10.0.1.0/24 / remote_ts 10.0.2.0/24

evidence.requirement: node3 and node4 reach each other via private addresses
evidence.summary: node3 (10.0.1.2) pings node4 (10.0.2.2) successfully and vice versa, 0% packet loss

evidence.requirement: traffic is encrypted in transit (no plaintext on transit network)
evidence.summary: swanctl CHILD_SA byte/packet counters increment with ping traffic; tcpdump on node1's transit interface (vtnet1) during a node3->node4 ping shows only ESP packets between 10.10.10.1 and 10.10.10.2, no 10.0.x.x plaintext

evidence.requirement: SSH/exec management access preserved throughout firewall reconfiguration
evidence.summary: Post rc.reload_all on both node1 and node2, exec commands succeed and show correctly assigned opt1/opt2 interfaces, confirming the default LAN allow rule kept management access intact

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime=1788626088 captured; shutdown -r acknowledged; post-restart kern.boottime=1788627593 (changed) with 15s uptime; IPsec SAs re-established and node3->node4 ping succeeds

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime=1788626087 captured; shutdown -r acknowledged; post-restart kern.boottime=1788627635 (changed) with 10s uptime; IPsec SAs re-established and node4->node3 ping succeeds

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id=47019498-16d3-4769-8a7d-b5372f7de78a captured; reboot issued; post-restart boot_id=3e4d9289-72fc-493c-b951-4fa39a638307 (changed) with 0min uptime; persisted /etc/network/interfaces restored eth1 addressing/route automatically and ping to node4 succeeds

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id=b1305252-e3b4-46c7-a8b9-529c675c0923 captured; reboot issued; post-restart boot_id=c5363588-b28d-470e-92d0-ce24d5acdd0d (changed) with 0min uptime; persisted /etc/network/interfaces restored eth1 addressing/route automatically and ping to node3 succeeds
